title: Open Values Lines v0.2
description: The list of rules a person can choose to hold, such as an allergy, a diet or a company to avoid, plus the published sets of rules that are on by default. Conscious Consuming keeps it.

format.description: Always "open-values-lines". Tells a reader that this file is the list of rules a person can hold.

version.description: The version of the lines format this file follows, 0.2.

updated.description: The day the file was last changed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

note.description: A paragraph for maintainers saying what the file holds and how the app reads it.

kinds.description: The kinds of rule, keyed by kind id (allergy, diet, require, avoid, cap, lean), each with one sentence saying what that kind of rule does.

sets.description: Published sets of rules that are switched on by default, such as the baseline. A person can read every rule in a set, switch a rule off for themselves, or copy the set and change it.

lines.description: Every rule a person can choose to hold, such as an allergy, a diet or a company to avoid. Rules are off until the person picks them.

id.description: The set's id, starting with "floor:", such as "floor:cc-shared-v1-pilot".

tier.description: Always "floor": a set that is on by default for everyone.

label.description: The set's name as shown to people, such as "The baseline".

version.description: The set's own version, as major.minor.patch with an optional suffix such as "-pilot". It changes whenever a rule changes.

published.description: The day this version of the set was first published, as YYYY-MM-DD.

status.description: Where the set stands: waiting for the founder's sign-off, published, or replaced by a newer set.

defaultOn.description: Always true: the set applies until a person switches it or one of its rules off.

presentation.description: Always "fold": options a rule matches are folded away under a heading the person can open, not removed.

unknownEvidence.description: Always "keep-visible": an option with no sourced claim on the rule's criterion stays in view. Only a sourced, dated claim can fold it.

namedConsumer.description: The parts of the app that read this set, named so a reader can check that something uses it.

maximumRules.description: The most rules the set may hold.

maximumExcludedSharePerCategory.description: The largest share of any one category's options the set may fold, as a fraction between 0 and 1, such as 0.25 for a quarter.

maximumExcludedShareOverall.description: The largest share of all options across the catalogue the set may fold, as a fraction between 0 and 1.

minimumRemainingPerCategory.description: The fewest options that must stay visible in any category after the set folds its matches.

minimumMatchesPerRule.description: The fewest options each rule must match. A rule that matches fewer fails the check.

bounds.description: Limits on how much the set may hide. research/lines_audit.js checks them against the live data and fails if the set goes over.

license.description: The licence the set is published under, such as "CC0-1.0".

portableRuleIds.description: Always true: rule ids stay the same in a copy, so a person's choices about a rule still apply there.

localRuleOverrides.description: Always true: a person can switch any single rule off for themselves without copying the set.

requiredAttribution.description: What a copy must keep, such as the source for every rule it retains.

fork.description: The terms for copying the set and changing it.

curator.description: Who looks after the set now.

status.description: The set's governance status, such as "published".

changePath.description: How someone can get the set changed.

noCapture.description: The rule that no sponsor or ranked company can pay to add, remove or weaken a rule.

governance.description: Who looks after the set and how it can be changed.

version.description: The set version this entry describes.

date.description: The day of the change, as YYYY-MM-DD.

changes.description: What changed in this version, in a sentence or two.

changelog.description: Every version of the set, newest first, with its date and what changed.

id.description: The rule's id, starting with "avoid:floor-", such as "avoid:floor-fossil-financing-banks". It stays the same in copies of the set.

kind.description: Always "avoid": the rule folds the options it matches.

tier.description: Always "floor": the rule belongs to a default-on set.

label.description: The rule's name as shown to people.

reads.description: One sentence saying exactly what the rule folds.

effect.description: Always "fold": a matched option is folded under a heading the person can open, not removed.

categories.description: The ids of the facts files the rule applies in, such as "banking".

type.description: Always "criterion-band": the rule matches on one criterion's score.

criterion.description: The key of the criterion the rule reads, such as "environment".

band.description: Always "poor": the band of scores the rule matches.

maximumExclusive.description: Always 20: a score must be below 20 to match.

requiresSource.description: Always true: a score with no source link does not match.

requiresAsOf.description: Always true: a score with no date does not match.

match.description: Which options the rule matches: those whose score on one criterion is in the Poor band and carries a source and a date.

note.description: One line saying what the source shows.

source.description: The web address of the source.

asof.description: When the source's claim was true, as a year, a year and month, or a full date.

receipt.description: The source behind the rule as a whole. Each matched option must still carry its own sourced, dated claim.

id.description: The rule's id: its kind, a colon, and a short name, such as "diet:vegan" or "avoid:nestle". A values file stores these ids when a person picks the rule.

kind.description: What the rule does. "allergy" keeps only options declared free of an allergen. "diet" and "require" keep only options with a matching label. "avoid" hides a company and its brands. "cap" (a price ceiling) and "lean" (a tie-breaker) are listed but not active yet.

label.description: The rule's name as shown to people, such as "Vegetarian".

reads.description: One sentence saying exactly what the rule does to the list.

tag.description: For allergy rules: the allergen tag, such as "nuts", that products are checked against. Only an explicit free claim for this tag keeps a product in view.

accept.description: For diet and require rules: the labels that satisfy the rule. An option passes when any of its labels (its focuses) is in this list, so "Vegan" also satisfies Vegetarian.

entity.description: For avoid rules: the id of the company to hide. An entry whose code equals this id is hidden.

why.description: For avoid rules: a web address that shows which brands the company owns.

brands.description: For avoid rules: the company's brand names, in lower case. An entry is hidden when one of these appears as a whole word in its brand, name or code.
